comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @Jerskouille, @bobylito and @pixelastic to be potential reviewers

I think I know what bugs me about this PR. While I do agree with you we should fix it at the source, I think this should be at the helper level.
Indeed, in the helper:
- `addNumericRefinement(attribute, operator, value)` type-checks value and convert it to a float if it's a string
- but `removeNumericRefinement(attribute, operator, value)` just does a simple `===` comparison

Which means that:

``` js
var val = /* ... */;
helper.addNumericRefinement('attribute', '=', val);
helper.removeNumericRefinement('attribute', '=', val);
```

is actually not guaranteed to work, which is, to me, weird.

By fixing this, we would actually fix the need for this PR.
That being said, the current issue underlined by @Jerskouille should be fixed in the helper because that's no consistent with the behavior we put.

I think that what is expected to be numeric should be parsed. The reason is that we have a serialized form that may cause the number to be transformed to string (url stuff) but for the sake of convenience we should provide numbers when we can (who wants to parse a value coming from a library?)

I'm fixing the bug you found @Jerskouille. I couldn't find the ticket on the helper, if there is one, can you reference it here?
@bobylito I didn't file one, I was waiting to see the end of this discussion. Now submitted here: https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/issues/285 .

This is currently an issue affecting users so gonna merge it, release and then once https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/pull/284 is merged and helper is released I will revert this commit.

title: fix(currentRefinedValues): clear numeric refinements using original value
